title: Capture harness calls main's private signal handlers and uses stringly-typed access instead of a public API
detail: _on_* handlers are private by GDScript convention and are signal-wiring details. main already exposes the public precedent request_connect; QoS apply/select bypassed it, so harness and tests couple to private wiring.
recommended_fix: Add public main.apply_qos(pipe_id, alloc, cls_lane) and main.select_pipe(pipe_id); make _on_pipe_selected/_on_qos_apply delegate. Capture (and tests) call the public API, and close via qos_panel.close_panel().

title: main._ready recomputes wedge_layout and node_placements despite doc claiming layout is computed once and threaded through
evidence:
_generate_world(WorldSeed.wedge_layout(SEED))
	sim = SimCore.new()
	sim.setup(SEED, WorldSeed.node_placements(SEED, WorldSeed.wedge_layout(SEED)))
--- against the doc at main.gd:140:
## "Regenerate Preview" both run exactly this. The layout is computed ONCE
## by the caller and threaded through, so staged nodes and sim placements
## can never drift onto different layouts.
detail: The stated invariant (single layout, threaded) is enforced only by function purity, not by code: layout runs twice, node_placements twice (again in _stage_nodes). Future non-pure changes could silently desync node_index from sim indices.
recommended_fix: In _ready: var layout := WorldSeed.wedge_layout(SEED); var placements := WorldSeed.node_placements(SEED, layout); pass placements into both _generate_world/_stage_nodes and sim.setup, matching the documented contract.

title: FlowView.pulse_egress maps sim node indices positionally onto scene-tree child order
detail: Implicit cross-module invariant: Nodes container child order must equal sim node index (established only by _stage_nodes appending in placement order). Any future out-of-order child or decoration node silently misroutes egress pulses.
recommended_fix: Look up sites by NodeSite.node_index (build an index-to-site map once in FlowView.setup) instead of positional get_child(i), making the binding explicit.

title: Pooled-capacity formula duplicated in QosPanel and SimCore
evidence:
scripts/qos_panel.gd:126:
		int(SimBalance.TIERS[p.tier].capacity_u_s) * int(p.parallel),
scripts/sim_core.gd:323:
		var pooled_units := int(SimBalance.TIERS[p.tier].capacity_u_s) * int(p.parallel)
detail: The bundling rule (capacity x parallel) lives in two modules. If pooling semantics change (e.g., a parallel efficiency penalty), the panel display drifts from sim truth silently.
recommended_fix: Expose one helper, e.g. SimCore.pooled_units(pipe_dict) (or store pooled capacity on the pipe dict), and have QosPanel display it instead of recomputing.

title: View palette colors (Color) embedded in the sim balance data module instead of the WorldSeed palette home
detail: Project palette tokens (COL_*) live in WorldSeed ("palette tokens only" doctrine in node_site.gd). Class colors in scripts/sim/ make pure-view consumers (FlowView dots, QosPanel swatch) depend on the sim data module for presentation constants.
recommended_fix: Move class colors to WorldSeed (e.g., COL_CLASS_EMAIL/COL_CLASS_STREAMING) or a view palette; keep SimBalance purely numeric sim tunables.

title: InputRouter now depends directly on FlowView, moving half the classification decision out of the pure static classify()
evidence:
@onready var flow_view: FlowView = get_node("../FlowView")
...
	_picked_pipe = flow_view.pick_pipe(screen_pos, camera)
	_mode = Mode.SELECT if _picked_pipe >= 0 else Mode.ORBIT
--- while the header still claims:
## The decision is factored into the static classify() so the headless suite
## can pin the contract.
detail: The router (input grammar module) now calls into a view sibling inside _begin, so the documented headless-pinnable contract covers only the physics half; SELECT needs a live scene (compensated by test_view_interaction's gesture legs).
recommended_fix: Acceptable tradeoff, but update the header to state classify() covers physics hits only, or inject the pipe picker (callable set by main) so the router stays view-agnostic.

title: Editor-capture harness code (~40 lines of viewport/camera/save plumbing) embedded in the composition root
detail: One-shot harness concerns (camera nudging, force_draw, PNG save, quit) live in main.gd, growing the composition root; the project already has a capture-harness home (capture_runner.gd, cmdline-activated).
recommended_fix: Once stable, extract the editor-shot path into a @tool helper (e.g., tools/editor_capture.gd) invoked by main, keeping the composition root to wiring and the shared generation body.
